name: hcapp_respondDirectMessageRequest
description: Accepts or declines a pending request to direct-message the caller (E9.F1.S19). A request is pending when the requester holds a HasherFriendMap row (UserId = requester, Friend_UserId = caller) with FriendSince NULL and Removed 0. Accept: both rows (created or revived) become friends — FriendSince set, Removed 0, a freshly minted ThreadId shared by both — and the requester is pushed '<name> accepted' (rowsets 2–3). Decline: the requester's row is marked Removed and they are told NOTHING — their app keeps saying 'requested'; a decline is final unless the caller later starts a DM with them. Auth: HC6.ValidateAppAuth (spNumber 131, @param NULL — a standard token). Permission gate: the request must be addressed to the token's user; nothing else. Uses the two-rowset error shape: {success 0, errorCode, errorType} then the standard error detail. Since 2026-10-13 a NULL @accept is refused (it passed NOT IN (0,1) and declined).

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Registered device UUID. Default NULL (ValidateAppAuth then fails gracefully).

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived token (standard, device secret; @param NULL). Default NULL.

parameters.name: fromPublicHasherId
parameters.description: The requester, by public id (resolved to Hasher.id; Removed hashers do not resolve). Required in effect: NULL, unknown, or no pending request from them → 2004.

parameters.name: accept
parameters.description: 1 accept, 0 decline. Has a SQL default of NULL but NULL is NOT handled: see code smells — a NULL @accept with a valid pending request falls through to the DECLINE branch.

rowsets.description: Auth failure only (ValidateAppAuth): the error detail is returned ALONE at index 0 and the SP returns.

rowsets.name: ErrorEnvelope
rowsets.description: Every other refusal: {success 0, errorCode, errorType} at index 0, then the StandardErrorResult detail at index 1. Codes: 2004 no such pending request — requester unknown, @accept out of range, or nothing pending ('That request is no longer waiting.', errorType 2); 2005 unhandled error from the CATCH (5).
Follows the ErrorEnvelope on every non-auth refusal.

rowsets.name: Result
rowsets.description: On success: the outcome and the other party, one row.

columns.name: ThreadId
columns.description: UPPER(new ThreadId) on accept; NULL on decline.

rowsets.name: PushDetail
rowsets.description: ACCEPT ONLY, API-only (stripped): what the shim needs to tell the requester. Absent on decline — the client reply has two rowsets, the API sees four only on accept.

columns.name: FromPublicHasherId
columns.description: UPPER(the CALLER's Hasher.PublicHasherId) — the accepter, who the push is from.

rowsets.name: Recipients
rowsets.description: ACCEPT ONLY, API-only (stripped): the requester's live devices (removed 0, FcmToken present, LastLogin within 180 days, build >= HC6.MinBuildForDmPush()). May be empty.

columns.name: BadgeTotal
columns.description: HC6.UserUnreadChatTotal for the requester; NULL when the device's build is below HC6.MinBuildForIconBadge().

sideEffects: Accept: MERGE HC.HasherFriendMap WITH (HOLDLOCK) for both directions (caller→requester, requester→caller) — UPDATE FriendSince = COALESCE(existing, now), ThreadId = new id, Removed 0, updatedAt; or INSERT (UserId, Friend_UserId, FriendSince, ThreadId). A previously ended or declined pair is revived with a NEW ThreadId, so earlier DM history (under the old ThreadId) is not shown in the new thread.
Decline: UPDATE HC.HasherFriendMap SET Removed 1, updatedAt on the requester's row (FriendSince IS NULL).
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on 2004 and in the CATCH (2005).
The API pushes 'dmAccepted' to rowset 3 on accept; nothing is queued in the database.

codeSmells.issue: Accept reads the requester's photo/name after the commit without re-checking Removed
codeSmells.detail: Line 84–85 and 89–91 read HC.Hasher for the result and push rows outside the transaction; harmless, noted only because @fromId was resolved with Removed = 0 at line 48 and a concurrent GDPR delete between the two would still return the row.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
